chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Three talents: why being only mediocre at each
summary: Late in tap, he says he was ahead because he could sing, dance and act, then calls himself mediocre at each in terms of pay.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: The thing that amazes me is that you started tap dancing
at such a late age. You became such an innovater so quickly.
But did you have any dancing --

Listen, that wasn't very quick. I had two points ahead of the game, see. See, I'm an actor, I'm a singer, I'm a dancer. Okay? The personality for singing, the personality for acting, the personality for dancing, that's three of them. Now, I've got three talents. Now how am I going to be so far behind? You ain't got but one. Or you ain't got but one. I got three. I sing, dance, talk and act. Now all those have got something to go with 'em. See what I mean? What boosted the dancing was the singing, what boosted the singing was the dancing, what boosted the acting was the personality. That's the way it developed itself. I ain't so far behind, I'm ahead. That's where I beat Fred Astaire, because I had much more to go with than he did. He could
only dance. I could sing and dance and act.
But the thing is you were great at all of that.
I don't know about the great part, just mediocre. Just use mediocre, it's a good word.
Mediocre, okay, mediocre at all of them.

Yeah, it took three of them to be mediocre, it took three of them. What's the difference of being great in all of them and successful in none. I can use the mediocre. So if you're going to give me a dollar and a quarter for a song when the song is worth $10 and $1.15 for a dance and the dance is worth $400, another guy is going to give me $1.25 for acting and acting is worth $450, everything is mediocre, ain't it?
